title: probes-are-a-nest-with-settled-in-preprocess
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
intention: The shim's at-rest probes are shaken as a nest whose preprocess sieve, settled, hands the record band only the probes whose watched tree moved since they last fired, so a settled probe costs the beat nothing and a quiet beat reads no corpus twice.
how: (1) each Probe declares (or defaults) the root it watches — `root` on the frozen dataclass, defaulting to the class-space repo root for a probe that names none, so no probe fires less than today; (2) shim.on_pulse builds a nest from its declared probes: subjects = {identity: probe}, one preprocess sieve settled(subjects) -> the identities whose tree_fingerprint(root) differs from the fingerprint stamped at their last fire (or never fired, or while_true), one record sieve trigger(probe) that is today's body (fires -> _fire -> gathered_enough) unchanged; the shake replaces the for-loop at shim.py:260, the held/fired/still_true bookkeeping stays; (3) the fingerprint at last fire is stamped in the shim's own memory beside _was_true/_cleared — instance state the holder owns (Law 6), lost on restart like _cleared, so a restart walks once; (4) proofs: nest tooth over a fixture shim (settled trigger not called; moved and never-fired called), zero-reads tooth, shim proofs resealed unchanged, does_a_beat_cost_what_changed's before/after numbers on the verdict; all under netns.
falsifier: DONE when (1) the at-rest probes are assembled through cairn/tools/base/nest.py as a nest whose subjects are the discovered probes and whose one PREPROCESS sieve, settled, receives the whole probe set and returns only those whose watched root moved since their last fire (tree_fingerprint) or that have never fired; the record band fires each returned probe's trigger exactly as on_pulse does today — one tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a fixture shim with three probes (one settled, one moved, one never fired) asserting the settled one's trigger is NOT called and the other two are; (2) a settled probe reads 0 files on the beat — measured by a tooth counting opens under a fixture root (strace-free: wrap Path.open / os.walk in the fixture); (3) the beat's wall time and file reads over the live 99 are measured before and after by does_a_beat_cost_what_changed (the existing probe) and the after reads fewer files on a quiet beat, with both numbers on the verdict — never a snapshot asserted in a proof; (4) the poke-per-crossing, while_true, cleared, enough, and first_seen semantics of on_pulse are byte-identical (the shim's own proofs reseal unchanged). RED if any probe's trigger fires less often than today when its root moved, or if a band is authored. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants every probe walked every beat regardless (his 'agreed on all counts' says settled probes are not walked).
traces_to: Law 1 (a probe re-deriving an unchanged corpus every beat is re-deriving the settled); memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll and ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat (the beat stays a pulse; the saving is in the shim's evaluation, not in the loop). Telos: the system's resting cost shrinks as it settles.
watchme: none, because the beat's own probe cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/probes/does_a_beat_cost_what_changed.py already measures beat cost every beat and is the instrument this ticket's verdict reads; a second probe would watch the watcher.
gates_bound: proof gate — nest tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a fixture shim (settled not called, moved and never-fired called), zero-reads tooth, the shim's existing proofs resealed unchanged; all under netns; hollow at HEAD reads no hollow file.

PROVED exit gate — the verdict artifact answers the validate berth's criteria by instrument, including before/after beat reads from does_a_beat_cost_what_changed.

cast_checks.assumption_check: THREE. (1) That every walking probe's watched root is nameable — measured at build over the 48 walkers (grep rglob/glob/os.walk/iterdir per module); a probe whose root cannot be named is never settled, so the assumption failing costs nothing but the saving. (2) That tree_fingerprint is cheaper than the walk it replaces — 5.9ms over 806 files (settled.py:66); the before/after read counts are the instrument, not the assumption. (3) That the shake ticket's preprocess contract (fire(name, subjects) -> subset) lands first — depends_on names it; this ticket does not build the contract.
cast_checks.missing_check: ONE point not wrapped, on purpose: persisting the last-fire fingerprint across restarts. Today _cleared is in-memory and lost on restart; the fingerprint stamp follows the same rule so a restart walks once — a persisted stamp is instance state under the holder and can come later against a measured need. Everything else is a decision line.
cast_checks.falsifier_check: DONE when (1) the at-rest probes are assembled through cairn/tools/base/nest.py as a nest whose subjects are the discovered probes and whose one PREPROCESS sieve, settled, receives the whole probe set and returns only those whose watched root moved since their last fire (tree_fingerprint) or that have never fired; the record band fires each returned probe's trigger exactly as on_pulse does today — one tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a fixture shim with three probes (one settled, one moved, one never fired) asserting the settled one's trigger is NOT called and the other two are; (2) a settled probe reads 0 files on the beat — measured by a tooth counting opens under a fixture root (strace-free: wrap Path.open / os.walk in the fixture); (3) the beat's wall time and file reads over the live 99 are measured before and after by does_a_beat_cost_what_changed (the existing probe) and the after reads fewer files on a quiet beat, with both numbers on the verdict — never a snapshot asserted in a proof; (4) the poke-per-crossing, while_true, cleared, enough, and first_seen semantics of on_pulse are byte-identical (the shim's own proofs reseal unchanged). RED if any probe's trigger fires less often than today when its root moved, or if a band is authored. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants every probe walked every beat regardless (his 'agreed on all counts' says settled probes are not walked).
cast_checks.collision_check: Over the whys. ground_loop charter (heartbeat + device list, THAT IS ALL) — untouched; the nest is the shim's. Probe charter (a declaration, frozen) — gains an optional root field with a default; the trigger predicate is unchanged. Law 6 — the fingerprint stamp is the holder shim's own memory. shim.py:271 _cleared-first — kept: cleared is checked before settled, so a retired probe is never fingerprinted. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
cast_checks.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs, and the ticket answers: WHERE is the loop to replace? shim.py:260 'for cb in declared:' inside on_pulse; the body from :275 (true_now = cb.fires) down is the record sieve verbatim. WHAT is the subject key? cb.identity (already the key of _cleared/_was_true). WHAT does settled return? [identity for identity, cb in subjects.items() if cb.while_true or identity not in self._last_fp or self._last_fp[identity] != tree_fingerprint(cb.root)]; a probe with root None is always returned. WHERE is the fingerprint stamped? in _fire, after the poke: self._last_fp[cb.identity] = tree_fingerprint(cb.root) if cb.root else None. WHAT does a settled probe look like in the pulse record? held.append({why, to, reason: 'settled — root unchanged since last fire'}). WHERE is Probe.root? cairn/tools/base/probe.py:303 dataclass, root: str | None = None, documented beside `enough`. HOW to measure before/after? run does_a_beat_cost_what_changed's carry over the live shim twice (two quiet beats) before the change and after; both on the verdict. WHAT NOT to touch: loop.py, discovery.py, the Probe trigger/carry/enough contract, _cleared semantics.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Considered wiring settled() into each of the 42 walking probes by hand — 42 edits that each new probe must remember; the nest does it once at the shim (Law 4: physics, not policy). Considered a cache inside Probe.fires — that hides the skip from the pulse record; a preprocess sieve stamps skipped_by so the skip is visible in the beat's held list.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: settled.py:86 is the memo and tree_fingerprint is the instrument (5.9ms over 806 files); does_a_beat_cost_what_changed already measures beat cost; nest.py is the shake word with a preprocess band nothing populates. Congruency lab: the ground_loop charter says the beat is a pulse and a device list, nothing more — this touches the shim, not the loop.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That a probe's trigger depends only on its watched tree — a trigger that reads the clock or the bus would be wrongly settled. Guard: a probe with root=None and no default walk is never settled (always returned by the preprocess sieve); the default root is the repo only for probes that walk it (measured at build: the 48 walkers, their roots named).
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat (CC-- x4): nothing changes in ground_loop; the nest lives in BaseShim.on_pulse. Law 7: a settled probe is held with reason 'settled — root unchanged since last fire', never silently absent from the pulse record. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.

decisions.text: BaseShim.on_pulse shakes its declared probes as a nest: subjects keyed by probe identity; one PREPROCESS sieve `settled` returns the identities to score; one RECORD sieve `trigger` is today's per-probe body (shim.py:275-300) verbatim. The for-loop at shim.py:260 becomes the shake.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 'agreed on all counts' on CC's proposal; measured 2026-09-16: ground_loop discovery.discover() finds 99 probes over 40 devices, 0 import failures (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovery.py:168); cairn/tools/base/shim.py:259-300 on_pulse evaluates every declared probe's trigger in turn each beat — the only skip is the in-memory _cleared set (shim.py:271, per shim, lost on restart); 48 of the 99 probe modules walk a tree (rglob/glob/os.walk/iterdir) in their trigger or carry; the memo tool cairn/tools/base/settled.py:86 settled(key, root, compute) — remembered until tree_fingerprint(root) changes, 5.9ms over 806 files — is used by 6 probes today and 42 walkers do not use it. (2026-09-15's note '~78 probes, Probe.settled() exists, none wired' is corrected by this measurement: it is the settled TOOL, and six are wired.)

decisions.text: settled returns a probe iff while_true, or never fired, or root is None, or tree_fingerprint(root) != the fingerprint stamped at its last fire. A settled probe's trigger is NOT called and it reads 0 files; it appears in the pulse record as held with reason 'settled — root unchanged since last fire'.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15: 'settled() exists and none are wired to it'; Law 7 (visible, never silent); settled.py:64 tree_fingerprint

decisions.text: Probe gains `root: str | None = None` — the tree it watches. A walking probe names its root at build (48 measured walkers); a probe that names none is never settled. No probe fires less often than today when its root moved.
decisions.by: CC 2026-09-16 unobjected; the hidden_assumption at birth (a clock- or bus-reading trigger must not be settled)

decisions.text: The last-fire fingerprint lives in the shim's memory beside _cleared and _was_true; a restart walks once. Persisting it is not built until a measured need.
Cleared is checked BEFORE settled: a retired probe is never fingerprinted.
decisions.by: shim.py:266-273 'CLEARED IS TERMINAL and is checked FIRST'

decisions.text: Measured done: beat wall time and file reads over the live probes on a quiet beat, before and after, read through does_a_beat_cost_what_changed and written on the verdict — never asserted as a number in a proof.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 'agreed on all counts' on the before/after measurement; memory proof-over-live-data-assert-invariants
